page: Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized server belonging to the Lasv4 family. It features 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is exceptionally large, offering 23038 GB of capacity with Premium Storage capability. The virtualization layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

In benchmark evaluations, the L96as_v4 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test, Geekbench multi-core score, and PassMark CPU score all rank in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory performance is also highly competitive, with small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth reaching 7287.47 GB/sec (top 10%) and large-block uncached read and write speeds placing in the top 25%. Database operations are robust, as evidenced by Redis SET operations achieving 122.77 million operations per second.

This server is highly suited for large-scale database deployments, data-intensive applications, and memory-heavy workloads that benefit from massive local storage and high-throughput memory. It excels in multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation and ray tracing, which both scored in the top 10%. However, single-threaded performance is relatively moderate, with gzip and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the average range. The absence of a dedicated GPU makes it less suitable for heavy GPU-accelerated deep learning training, though it maintains strong CPU-based LLM inference capabilities for small to medium models.
